title: ci(lint): report how many gates never ran when Lint & Repo Gates aborts
body:
Closes #17382

Clause-②: no

`Lint & Repo Gates` runs its gates as a sequence of Actions steps and stops at
the first non-zero exit. That abort is deliberate and adjudicated — the
`GATE ORDER IS DELIBERATE` note above `jobs:` in `lint.yml` carries a
maintainer ruling (#13690, 2026-09-03) and even names the quantity the ordering
is tuned to shrink: **"the unmeasured tail"**. Nothing anywhere computed it.

This PR computes it. Fail-fast is untouched, no gate moved, no
`continue-on-error` anywhere.

## The card's premise, re-measured — and narrowed

The card says the gates are "`bash -e` 下的顺序步骤" and that the output contains
"没有任何东西说它们没跑" (nothing that says they did not run). **Measured on
`origin/main` at `d46deba195`, both halves need correcting, and the second one
narrows the defect. The narrowed claim is what this PR rests on.**

The gates are not lines in one `bash -e` script: the `lint` job declares **168
separate `- name:` steps** (6 setup + 1 gate-family selector + 161 gates). The
abort mechanism is Actions step sequencing. That difference matters, because it
changes what a reader receives — measured on three surfaces separately, against
run 34468505490 (job 102842713265, `Lint & Repo Gates`, failed at step #55):

| surface | does it say the rest did not run? | does it give a count? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Actions Web UI / jobs API `steps[]` | **yes** — 112 declared steps came back `conclusion: "skipped"` | **no**, and `"skipped"` is also the word for a step its own `if:` turned off, so the one surface that says it cannot tell the two apart |
| check-run `output` | **no** — `title`, `summary`, `text` all `null`; only `annotations_count: 1`, the failing gate's own. `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` appears **0** times in `lint.yml`, so there is no writer for that surface | no |
| job log (what an API/agent reader consumes) | **no** — the log ends with the failing gate's output, `Process completed with exit code 1`, `Post job cleanup`. Not one line about the 112 behind it | no |

⇒ **The honest defect is not "nothing says it". It is: no surface anywhere
carries a COUNT, and the two surfaces read by the API and by this repo's own
agent seats carry nothing at all.** That is still the card's acceptance #1.

Two more readings taken at the same time: `continue-on-error` appears **0** times
as a key in `lint.yml` (one occurrence, in prose inside a comment), and
`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` **0** times.

## The card's second measurement: are there real inter-gate dependencies?

Probed statically over the 168 steps, in five edge kinds, **with a positive
control** — the probe had to find a dependency known to exist before its zero
could mean anything:

| edge kind | found |
|:--|:--|
| ① `steps.<id>.outputs.*` consumption | **5** — all from step 7 `Select the gate families this run pays for` (`id: gate-families`) into the `if:` of five later gates. **This is the positive control: a real, known dependency the probe reaches.** |
| ② `$GITHUB_ENV` / `$GITHUB_PATH` / `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` writes | 1, in setup step 4 (`Get pnpm store directory`) |
| ③ job-level `env` | none declared |
| ④ `run:` bodies redirecting output to a repo path | 0 |
| ⑤ gate steps whose `run:` could mutate the tree (`gen:`/`regen`/`--write`/`--fix`/`sed -i`/`mv`/`cp`/`tee`) | 1 candidate — `os-regen-merge self-test`, matched on the word "regen" in a script name, not on an observed write |

**Between the 161 gate steps themselves: zero edges.** Every dependency found
runs from the seven preamble steps into the gates, never gate-to-gate.

⛔ **Boundary, stated so the zero is not over-read:** this probe is static and
structural. It cannot see a dependency mediated by an unnamed side effect on the
working tree. Kind ④/⑤ are proxies for that, not proofs. The reading is
therefore "no declared inter-gate dependency", not "no dependency can exist" —
and it is reported for the record, because **this PR does not need it**: it keeps
fail-fast, so nothing here can produce the cascading false reds that making all
gates run would risk.

## What this adds

* `scripts/report-unmeasured-gate-tail.mjs` — asks the jobs API for this run's
  own job and counts three populations apart: what ran, what its own `if:`
  turned off *before* the failure (a deliberate absence), and what is *behind*
  the failure (the unmeasured tail). Prints the count and **every** un-run gate
  by name to the job log, to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and as one machine-readable
  line, plus a single `notice` annotation carrying that line.
* Two steps at the end of the `lint` job, both `if: failure()` — an offline
  self-test and the reporter — and `actions: read` on the job (read-only, and
  the only permission change).

Design points worth a reviewer's eye:

* **It never fails the job and never downgrades anything.** It runs only when the
  job is already failed and always exits 0; a non-zero exit there would only add
  a second annotation pointing at the reporter instead of at the gate. It emits a
  `notice`, never a `warning` or `error` — on an already-failed check a notice can
  be read neither as a pass nor as a downgrade. There is no `continue-on-error`.
* **When it cannot measure, it says NOT MEASURED and names the reason** rather
  than printing `0`. That distinction is the whole subject of the card.
* **It never truncates the list** it is about. A report on an unmeasured tail that
  ends in "… and 94 more" has reproduced the defect one level up.
* **It hardcodes no job `name:`.** It finds its own job by `runner_name`
  (= `RUNNER_NAME`), so the required-status-check context literal that `lint.yml`
  pins is not copied anywhere and a rename cannot make the reporter silently stop
  matching.

## Acceptance, measured on real runs

The probe branch `claude/issue-17382-tail-probe` (deleted) carried **two
independent planted failures**: a broken docs anchor (reds gate step #9, the
first gate) and an unquoted workflow step name (reds a gate ~160 steps behind
it). Its `lint.yml` blob was byte-identical to `origin/main`'s in the ablated
state — verified by `git hash-object`.

**1. Positive — run [34585740119](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34585740119) (job 103219414669).** Failed at step #9. The job log now ends:

```
  failed at step #9: Docs anchors resolve to real headings
  declared steps in this job:            170
  ran before the failure:                7
  turned off by their own condition:     0
  NEVER RAN (the unmeasured tail):       161
  ...
    - Unquoted workflow step names do not silently truncate at " #" (#15149)
    - Duration-shaped spec keys carry their unit in the key name
    - Unmeasured-gate-tail reporter self-test

  unmeasured-gate-tail: measured=yes never_ran=161 failed=1 ran=7 skipped_by_condition=0 declared=170 failed_at_step=9
```

The reader learns from one job run that 161 gates are unmeasured — including the
one carrying the second planted bug, named in the list.

**2. Negative control — run [34586827251](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34586827251) (job 103222868848), this branch, all green.**
`Lint & Repo Gates` = **success**, 173 steps success, exactly 2 skipped: both new
steps. `started_at == completed_at` on both. check-run `annotations_count: 0`;
`output.title` / `summary` / `text` all `null`; the log goes straight from the
last gate to `Post job cleanup`.

⇒ **zero new bytes on a green run** — no log output, no summary, no annotation.
Literal byte-identity between two *different* runs is not achievable (timestamps,
shas, cache keys differ), so the claim made and measured here is the one that
matters: this change contributes nothing to a green run's output. That is also
why the self-test step carries `if: failure()` — running it unconditionally
would have printed one line on every green run, and one line is still new noise.

**3. No downgrade.** `continue-on-error` count in `lint.yml`: 0 before, 0 after.
Every gate's exit code still decides the job.

**4. Ablation — run [34589155445](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34589155445) (job 103230201133).** Same
double-failure head, change removed (`lint.yml` restored to the `origin/main`
blob, script deleted). Result: failed at step #9, 162 steps `skipped`,
`annotations_count: 1` (the failing gate's own), `output.summary: null`, and
nothing anywhere about the 162 gates that never ran. Acceptance #1 reverts
exactly.

## Two defects the live runs caught that reasoning did not

Recorded because both were invisible offline, and both are now pinned:

1. **Run [34583803573](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34583803573) printed `never_ran=12` for a tail of 161.** The reporter runs
   while the job is still in progress, and the runner stamps `skipped` on the
   steps behind the failure *progressively* — at that instant only 12 carried the
   word. Counting `conclusion === 'skipped'` produced a lower bound on a lower
   bound, wearing the look of a precise number. Behind the failure the tail is now
   counted by **position**, and `conclusion` may only subtract steps that
   demonstrably ran. A mid-run fixture pins it.
2. **Run [34584689309](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34584689309) ended its own report with `- Report how many gates never
   ran`** — the step that was printing it, because the API had not yet marked it
   `in_progress`. The workflow now hands the step its own name via
   `OS_TAIL_REPORT_STEP`, and that the two lines agree is not left to a comment:
   `wiringVerdict()` reads `lint.yml` as text and the self-test fails on a stale
   value, a missing one, or a rename. Reverse-verified — mutated the env value on
   disk (blob `135f9caa` → `5f57f8e7`), self-test went red naming the drift,
   restored via `git checkout HEAD --`, blob back to `135f9caa`, `git diff HEAD`
   empty, self-test green again.

## Local verification

* `node scripts/report-unmeasured-gate-tail.mjs --self-test` — 32 assertions,
  exit 0. Driven over recorded jobs-API shapes, and separately validated against
  five real recorded jobs of this workflow (tails of 112, 109, 14, 0 and 161).
* `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 56 families; all 56 run
  with exit codes recorded and reconciled via `--ran`: **55 green, 1 NOT
  MEASURED** — `pnpm check:type-check-debt` exits 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: the
  workspace type closure is not built locally; `lint.yml` builds it before that
  step). Not a finding, and unrelated to this diff.
* `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config` over the whole repo — **6624 files, 0
  errors, 0 warnings, exit 0**. Not narrowed; the full population ran.
* Gate list re-derived at the final head: unchanged.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`, measured rather than assumed: walked 77 workspace manifests
(70 non-private) and **no** `files[]` entry can carry root `scripts/` or
`.github/`; the root manifest is `private: true`. Nothing published moves. The
label is applied on the PR.

## Deliberately not touched

* The `lint` job's `name:` — it is the required-status-check context.
* Gate order — the #13690 ruling forbids re-sorting.
* `lint.yml:135`'s "~70 sequential gate steps" prose (the real count is 168).
  Unenforced stale prose, ruled not a finding for this PR; left alone.
* One comment *was* amended, because this PR falsifies its wording: the
  duration-unit-keys step's "Placed LAST in this job" now reads "Placed LAST
  AMONG THE GATES", since two non-gate steps now follow it. The ruling it
  describes — nothing behind it is masked by its red — is untouched and still
  true: neither new step is a gate, and neither can be masked.
